data.title: Tigermed Directors Face Regulatory Warning and Fines Over Disclosure Lapses
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Hangzhou Tigermed Consulting Co., Ltd. Class H ( (HK:3347) ).

Hangzhou Tigermed Consulting has disclosed that its directors and controlling shareholders, Mr. Ye Xiaoping and Ms. Cao Xiaochun, have received a formal warning letter from the Zhejiang arm of the China Securities Regulatory Commission for failing to promptly disclose a 1% reduction in their A-share holdings made in December 2022. The warning will be logged in market integrity records, and the pair have been instructed to improve their understanding of securities rules, standardize trading and disclosure practices, and submit a written report within ten working days.

Separately, the Zhejiang Regulatory Bureau issued an advance notice of administrative penalty over a failure by the same shareholders to timely report a cumulative 5% change in their voting stake dating back to September 2019, deeming the lapse a violation of China’s Securities Law. Regulators plan to impose a warning and a fine of RMB500,000 on each individual, underscoring heightened enforcement of disclosure obligations for major shareholders and raising governance and compliance considerations for investors in the company.

data.title: Longhui International Widens Interim Loss as Revenue Falls
data.description:
Longhui International Holdings Ltd. ( (HK:1007) ) just unveiled an update.

Longhui International Holdings Ltd. reported unaudited interim results for the six months ended 30 June 2025, highlighting a challenging period for its restaurant-focused food and beverage business in mainland China. Revenue declined to RMB19.7 million from RMB29.4 million a year earlier, reflecting weaker sales and a leaner cost base driven by lower spending on consumables, staff and rental expenses.

Despite cost reductions, the group’s operating loss widened to RMB7.3 million from RMB4.4 million, with total loss for the period rising to RMB7.9 million versus RMB5.6 million previously. Finance costs eased, and a positive currency translation difference reduced the total comprehensive expense to RMB5.8 million, but the continuing losses underscore ongoing pressure on profitability and signal persistent challenges for stakeholders in the company’s turnaround efforts.

data.title: CCT Fortis Seeks Three-Year Extension and Zero-Interest Terms on 2025 Convertible Bonds

The move directly addresses near-term refinancing pressure by extending the company’s debt maturity profile and reshaping incentives for conversion into equity.

Because the bondholders are connected parties controlled by the company’s major shareholders, the changes constitute a connected transaction and are subject to Hong Kong Listing Rules, including Stock Exchange approval for the amendments and for listing the potential conversion shares, as well as independent shareholders’ approval, highlighting governance and minority investor considerations.
